lawyer: Md. Serajul Huq with S.A.M. Mahbub Elahi ------- For the Petitioner.
parties:
Md. Nurul Haque ------ Petitioners.
Vs.
Sonali Bank of Bangladesh & anr. ------ Respondents.
full_judgment:
This application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure at the instance of the defendant No. 1 petitioner Md. Nurul Hoque is directed against Order No. 23 dated 14.9.86 passed by Mr. Soumendera Sarker, Subordinate-Judge, Rajbari in Misc. Case No 13 of 1986 arising out of Money Suit No. 1 of 1985 allowing the said Misc. Case and vacating the earlier order dated 10.2.86 dismissing the suit for default and restoring the Money Suit No. 1 of 1981 to its original file and number. 

 2. Plaintiff-opposite party No.1 Sonali Bank, represented by the Branch Manager Sonali Bank,  Rajbari instituted Money Snit No. 8 of 1979 in the first Court of Subordinate judge, Faridpur against petitioner-defendant No. 1 Nurul Hoque (Ex-Deputy Chief Cashier, Sonali Bank, Rajbari Branch and defendant opposite party No. 2 Md. Shamsul Haque (Ex-Chief Accountant, Sonali Bank, Rajbari Branch- praying for a decree of Tk. 100,000 (one lac) against the defendant on the allegation that the defendant No. 1 was serving as Deputy Chief Cashier and defendant No. 2 was serving as Deputy Chief Accountant of Rajbari Branch of Sonali Bank. Defendant No. 1 Nurul Hoque and defendant No. 2 Md. Shamsul Haque were the joint custodians of the cash of the strong room of the said Rajbari Branch of the Sonali Bank. Gopal Chandra Sarker, Asstt. Cashier of the Bank of Rajbari Branch defalcated Tk. 81,508/- on 4.8.78 from the counter but defendant No. 1 Nurul Hoque, the Deputy Chief Cashier strangely did not detect the said fact. Defendant No. 1 Nurul Haque on the contrary deposited the entire defalcated amount with the plaintiff bank on the same day when detected and Asstt. Cashier Gopal Chandra Barker remained untraceable from that date 4.7.78. For this reason Defendant No. 1 Md. Nurul Huque was transferred to the Regional Office, Faridpur and Aminul Islam was posted as Chief Cashier of the plaintiff bank. Mr. Aminul Islam pressed hard asking the defendant No. 1 Nurul Hoque to hand over the charge of the cash and strong room but the defendant No. 1 was reluctant to hand over the charge of the same. Mr. Aminul Islam began to take over the charge from defendant No. 1 and on 2.10.78 the strong room was opened by defendant No. 1 Nurul Hoque and defendant No. 2 Md. Shamsul Haque and With the said two defendants Mr, Aminul Islam entered into the strong room with a view to verify the case of the strong room in the process of taking over charge It was detected that 2000 pieces of 50 taka notes amounting to Taka. 1,00,000/- (Taka one lac only) in two bundles were not found in the almirah. The matter was brought to the notice of the Bench Manager who personally verified the same and also found that the said 7000 pieces of 50A Taka notes were not anywhere in the strong room. 

 3. Defendant No. 1 Nurul Hoque did not give any explanation of such shortage of fifty taka notes. As defendant No. 1 Nurul Hoque and defendant No. 2 Md. Shamsul Haque were joint custodians of the cash of the strong room, defendant No 1 in collusion with defendant No. 2 Md. Shamsul Haque misappropriated the said amount of Tk. 100,000/-. The plaintiff Bank lodged PI R. on 3 10.78 with the police which gave rise to Special Case No. 11 of 1979. The DAB. investigated into the case and submitted charge sheet under section 409/467/109 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of Act II of 1947. The plaintiff Bank instituted the present suit on 10.7.79 The additional Division Special Judge, Dhaka, camp Faridpur tried the Special Case and acquitted both the defendants 1 and 2 of the charges on 26.4.84. The prosecution preferred an appeal to the High Court Division on 10.8.86. The appeal in the High Court Division has been numbered as Criminal Appeal No. 12 of 1986 and is pending for admission. in the present Money Suit 8 of 1979 the plaintiff was taking adjournments on the grounds that the relevant papers required for establishing the plaintiff's case against the defendants are with the prosecution or with the Court in the aforesaid Criminal Case. Mr. Abdul Hannan, Subordinate judge, Rajbari by order No. 13 dated 10.2.86 rejected the prayer made on behalf of the plaintiff Small Bank to stay further proceeding of the suit for giving the plaintiff Bank opportunity to bring relevant papers. Thereafter on the same day the learned Subordinate Judge passed order No. 14 dated 10.2.86 as follows : 

 4. Thereafter the plaintiff Sonali Bank filed a petition under Order 9, rule 9 C.P.C. for setting aside the impugned order of dismissal and restoration of the original suit. Soumendra Sarker, Subordinate Judge, Rajbari heard the Misc, Case No. 13 of 3986. In his Court one witness was examined on behalf of the plaintiff Bank and some documents were exhibited to show that the necessary papers were lying with the Deputy Attorney General (Criminal), Dhaka for filing an appeal against the order of acquittal passed in Special case No. 11 of 1979. The learned Subordinate Judge held that the view taken by his predecessor in the order No. 14 dated 10.2.86 that the petition for adjournment filed by the plaintiff is malafide and motivated is not correct as the plaintiff Bank has no personal grudge against any of the defendants. He found from the various exhibits such as the letter of the Asstt. Secretary, Ministry of Law (Ext. 1 (A), letter of the Department of Anti-corruption Ext. A (B) and the pendency of Govt. Appeal No. 12 of 1986 that the plaintiff petitioner had sufficient genuine ground for praying for adjournment as the suit could not proceed without those essential documents. The learned Subordinate Judge took the view that in the facts and circumstances of the case for the ends of justice the order of dismissal should be vacated and accordingly he set aside the order of dismissal and restored the suit to its original file and number. 

 5. The learned advocate for the defendant petitioner submits that the learned Subordinate Judge acted illegally in allowing the Miscellaneous case under Order 9, rule 9 C.P.C. without any finding that the plaintiff was prevented by sufficient cause for his non-appearance when the suit was called on for hearing. 

 6. He also submits that the order of dismissal was note under Order 9, rule 8 C.P.C. but should be deemed to be an order under Order 17, rule 3 C.P.C. and that therefore the remedy of the plaintiff did not lie under Order 9, rule 9 C.P.C. As already stated above, the plaintiff Bank's engaged advocate on very cogent grounds filed petition on 10.2.86 praying for adjournment as the relevant documents necessary for establishing plaintiff's case were with the prosecution in connection with the aforesaid Criminal case. The learned subordinate Judge in both the order Nos. 13 and 14 dated 10.2 86 rejected the prayer for adjournment made by the engaged advocate on behalf of the plaintiff. The learned subordinate Judge did not dismiss the suit on merit stating that plaintiff's suit is dismissed for want of evidence or for the failure of the plaintiff to establish his case by adducing any oral or documentary evidence. The learned Subordinate Judge rejected the petition for adjournment and dismissed the suit for default. It, therefore, cannot be said to be a dismissal on merit under Order 17, rule 3 C.P.C. It is apparent that after rejection of the prayer for adjournment when the suit was called on for hearing the plaintiff did not appear within the meaning of Order 9 Rule 8 read with Order 17 rule 2 C.P.C. and the learned Subordinate Judge dismissed the suit for default. It has been held in the cases of Satish Vs. Apara, 34 Cal 403 Bejoy Vs. Satish, 9 LC. 842, Sikandar Vs. Kashal, 59 Cal 756, Sardar Vs Jahar, 59 Cal 906, Baijnath Vs. Kedar, AIR 1938 Cal 74, Gopala Vs. Maria, 30 Madras 274, Ganesh Vs Baikunthes, AIR. 1951 P 291 that when an advocate stating grounds prays for an adjournment which is refused but has no further instructions to represent his client, there is no "appearance" and these decisions are in conformity with the decision in the case of Robinson Vs. Chad wick (1878) 7 Ch D 873 where counsel for the plaintiff expressed his inability to proceed on rejection of a prayer for an adjournment and Fry, J. held that he could only treat the case as if the plaintiff had not appeared at the trial. Further if the impugned Judgment is read as a whole it will be found that it is not corset that the learned subordinate judge did not find in his judgment and order dated 14.9.86 in Misc. ease No. 13 of 1986 that the plaintiff was prevented by sufficient cause from appearing when the suit was called on for bearing as in the said judgment and order dated 14.9.86 the learned Subordinate Judge has elaborately discussed the evidence on record and found that it was genuinely not possible for the plaintiff to appear in the suit without the relevant connected papers and registers relating to the alleged misappropriated amount of money which were seized by the D.A.B. and were with the prosecution in the Connected criminal case. This was the sufficient cause Which prevented the plaintiff from appearing in the Court when the suit was called on for hearing. 

 7. The supreme consideration for a Court of law is to do justice between the parties. In the absence of special reasons the courts of law have always leaned in favour of deciding disputes on merit affording both the parties opportunity to substantiate their version of the case. There is nothing to show that in the present case the plaintiff was negligent or was harassing the defendants unnecessarily. Since the learned Subordinate Judge has not committed any error of law occasioning failure of justice, we find no ground whatsoever calling for our interference under section 115(1) CPC.
